This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–5} The apparent meaning is that the thing sworn about is the thing sworn by, and this is permissible and commonly used when the matter is clear and important, as it is in this place. Allah swears by the dawn (al-Fajr), which is the end of the night and the beginning of the day, because in the passing of the night and the coming of the day there are signs that point to the perfection of Allah's power, and that He is the One who governs all affairs, the One to whom worship alone is due. In the dawn there is a virtuous and honoured prayer (the Fajr prayer), which is fitting for Allah to swear by. For this reason He swears next by the ten nights, which, according to the correct view, are either the ten nights of Ramadan or the ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah. These are nights that include virtuous days, and they contain acts of worship and drawing near to Allah that do not occur at other times. In the ten nights of Ramadan is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), which is better than a thousand months, and in its day is the fasting of the last part of Ramadan, which is one of the great pillars of Islam. In the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah is the Standing at Arafah, on which Allah forgives His servants with a forgiveness that grieves Satan, for Satan is never seen more humiliated, more repelled, than on the Day of Arafah, because of what he sees of the descent of the angels and the mercy of Allah upon His servants. Many of the rites of Hajj and Umrah also take place in these days. These are great matters, deserving that Allah swear by them.

{And by the night when it passes} (idha yasr); that is, at the time of its passing and its drawing its darkness over the servants, so that they settle, rest and become tranquil, out of His mercy and wisdom.

{Is there in that} mentioned {an oath for one of understanding?} (dhi hijr); that is, for one of intellect? Yes, a part of it suffices for one who has a heart, or who gives ear while being a witness.

This surah is Meccan.

The Most High says: ﴿Have you not considered﴾, with your heart and insight, ﴿how your Lord dealt with﴾ these tyrannical nations: ʿAd, and ﴿Iram, the people of the pillars﴾, the well-known tribe in Yemen, ﴿with lofty pillars﴾, meaning great strength, arrogance, and tyranny; ﴿the like of whom had not been created in the lands﴾, meaning in all the lands, in strength and might. Their prophet Hud, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah, and increased you in stature, broadly. So remember the bounties of God that you may prosper﴾. ﴿And Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley﴾, meaning the Wadi al-Qura. They hewed out the rocks with their strength and made them dwellings. ﴿And Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾, meaning lord of the armies who firmly established his kingdom as stakes firmly fix what is to be held in place. ﴿Who transgressed in the lands﴾. This description applies to ʿAd, Thamud, Pharaoh, and those who followed them, for they transgressed in the lands of God and harmed the servants of God in their religion and their worldly affairs. Therefore He said: ﴿So they multiplied corruption therein﴾, which is acting in disbelief and its branches, from all kinds of sins, and they strove to fight the messengers and turn people away from the path of God. When they reached such a level of arrogance as necessitated their destruction, God sent down upon them a portion of His punishment and a whip of torment. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ over those who disobey Him; He gives them respite for a while, then seizes them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

{15–20} He (Exalted is He) informs us about the nature of man as such: that he is ignorant and wrongdoing, with no knowledge of the outcomes. He supposes that the state he is in will continue and will not pass away, and he supposes that Allah's honouring him in this world and His bounty upon him indicate his nobility [in His sight] and nearness to Him. And when He "restricts his provision" (qadara ʿalayhi rizqahu), i.e., narrows it so that it no longer exceeds his sustenance, he supposes that this is a humiliation from Allah toward him. So Allah refutes this assumption, saying: "Nay" (kallā), i.e., it is not the case that everyone whom I have bestowed favours upon in this world is noble in My sight, nor that everyone whose provision I have restricted is despised before Me. Rather, wealth and poverty, abundance and constraint, are a trial from Allah and a test by which He tests His servants, to see who will stand before Him in gratitude and patience, so that He rewards such a one with a great reward, and (sends to) the one who is not like that a painful punishment, (ʿadhāb) (waby). Also, the aspiration of a servant that stops at the desire of his own self alone is a weakness of aspiration. For this reason Allah reproached them for their lack of concern for the circumstances of the needy creatures, saying: "Nay, but you do not honour the orphan" — the one who has lost his father and his earner and needs his heart to be consoled and kindness shown to him. You do not honour him; rather, you humiliate him. This indicates the absence of mercy in your hearts and the absence of desire for good. "And you do not urge one another to feed the poor (miskīn)," i.e., none of you urges the others to feed the needy among the poor and the destitute, and that is due to stinginess toward the world and its intense love, which is firmly rooted in the hearts. For this reason He said: "And you devour the inheritance (turāth)," i.e., the wealth left behind, "with greedy devouring (aklan lammā)," i.e., rapaciously, leaving nothing of it, "and you love wealth with abundant love (ḥubban jammā)," i.e., intensely. This is like His saying: "Rather, you prefer the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring" and "Nay, but you love the hasty (world) and leave the Hereafter."

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 89, verses 21–30:

{21–24} {Kallā} (No!); meaning: not everything you have loved of wealth and competed for of pleasures will remain for you. Rather, before you is a great Day and a mighty terror, on which the earth and the mountains and whatever is upon them will be leveled, until it is made a smooth, level plain, in which there is no crookedness and no elevation. Allah will come to judge between His servants, in shadows of clouds, and the noble angels of all the heavens will come {ṣaffan ṣaffā} (rank upon rank); meaning: row after row, each heaven's angels coming in rows, surrounding those below them of creation. These rows are rows of submission and humility before the Mighty King. {And Hell will be brought forth that Day}: it will be led by the angels with chains. So when these matters occur, {on that Day man will remember}: what he sent forth of good and evil, {but how will the remembrance benefit him?}: its time has passed and its era has gone. {He will say}, regretful over what he neglected concerning Allah: {"Oh, I wish I had sent forth [good deeds] for my life"}: the enduring, everlasting life, with righteous deeds; as Allah the Exalted said: {"He will say, 'Oh, I wish I had taken a way with the Messenger. Woe to me! I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend.'"} In this is evidence that the life which one should strive to perfect and attain, and to complete its pleasures, is the life in the abode of permanence, for it is the abode of eternity and everlastingness.

{25–26} {So on that Day, none will punish as He punishes}: for those who neglected that Day and forgot to work for it. {And none will bind as He binds}; for they will be bound with chains of fire, dragged on their faces through the boiling water, and then in the Fire they will be kindled. This is the recompense of the criminals.

{27–30} As for one who believed in Allah, was at peace with Him, and affirmed His messengers, it will be said to him: {"O reassured soul"}: at rest in the remembrance of Allah, tranquil in His love, whose eye is comforted by Allah. {"Return to your Lord"}: who nurtured you with His blessings, [and bestowed upon you of His goodness that by which you became among His friends and beloved ones], {well-pleased and pleasing}; meaning: pleased with Allah and with what He honored her with of reward, and Allah is pleased with her. {"So enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise."} This is addressed to the soul on the Day of Resurrection, and it is addressed to it at the time of the death-agony and death.

And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend.'"} In this is evidence that the life which one should strive to perfect and attain, and to complete its pleasures, is the life in the abode of permanence, for it is the abode of eternity and everlastingness.

{25–26} {So on that Day, none will punish as He punishes}: for those who neglected that Day and forgot to work for it. {And none will bind as He binds}; for they will be bound with chains of fire, dragged on their faces through the boiling water, and then in the Fire they will be kindled. This is the recompense of the criminals.

{27–30} As for one who believed in Allah, was at peace with Him, and affirmed His messengers, it will be said to him: {"O reassured soul"}: at rest in the remembrance of Allah, tranquil in His love, whose eye is comforted by Allah. {"Return to your Lord"}: who nurtured you with His blessings, [and bestowed upon you of His goodness that by which you became among His friends and beloved ones], {well-pleased and pleasing}; meaning: pleased with Allah and with what He honored her with of reward, and Allah is pleased with her. {"So enter among My servants. And enter My Paradise."} This is addressed to the soul on the Day of Resurrection, and it is addressed to it at the time of the death-agony and death.

And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 89, verses 21–30:

{21–24} {Kallā} (No!); meaning: not everything you have loved of wealth and competed for of pleasures will remain for you. Rather, before you is a great Day and a mighty terror, on which the earth and the mountains and whatever is upon them will be leveled, until it is made a smooth, level plain, in which there is no crookedness and no elevation. Allah will come to judge between His servants, in shadows of clouds, and the noble angels of all the heavens will come {ṣaffan ṣaffā} (rank upon rank); meaning: row after row, each heaven's angels coming in rows, surrounding those below them of creation.
